visual_evidence.method: Separate deterministic five-second 1280x720 Metal captures at scalability 2 use the same fixed camera and the same solver-selected side-camera preset. Metrics are descriptive and are not photoreal acceptance thresholds.

solver_side_camera.finding: The masked membrane does not introduce a translucent dome, card, gray band, or repeated tent in the close view, but its added volume is subtle from this angle.

visual_evidence.finding: The retained membrane gives the primary approach crest a denser, connected foam-lace structure without reviving the rejected shell artifacts. It remains too subtle and too dependent on the analytical base swell to qualify as a photoreal overturning hydraulic.

remaining_photoreal_defects: The strongest rapid still reads primarily as a broad analytical swell rather than a fully resolved overturning hydraulic.
The masked plunge face is subtle in close side view and does not yet provide a convincing aerated hole or recirculating entrained-air volume.
Niagara still reads as sprite breakup instead of collision-aware spray and mist tied to a high-resolution free-surface simulation.
The source hydraulics remain procedural reference data rather than measured seasonal Zambezi behavior.
Terrain, waterline, ecology, raft, equipment, character animation, and final occlusion remain below the lifelike target.
A target-hardware GPU profile and named art review have not accepted the combined surface, masked curtain, and Niagara composition.
